title: Task-structured modularity emerges in artificial networks and aligns with brain architecture
title_zh: 任务结构化模块性在人工网络中出现并与脑结构一致
abstract: Understanding how neural systems develop modular organization is fundamental to both neuroscience and artificial intelligence. Modular architectures are thought to be critical for adaptability and complex cognitive performance by enriching the brain’s ability to integrate and process information. While prior work posits that modularization emerges from physical constraints, such as minimizing metabolic wiring costs, these spatial models alone do not fully explain the functional organization of brain networks. A critical, unanswered question is how the functional demands of learning complex tasks computationally influence network topology. Here we demonstrate, using recurrent neural networks trained on cognitive tasks, how functional demands shape structural organization. We find that multitask learning paradigms enhance network modularity compared with single-task training, especially when task load strains the network’s capacity. Networks trained with incremental multitask learning, in particular, develop the highest degree of modularity and maintain superior performance. Furthermore, these task-induced networks exhibit structural properties that more closely resemble biological brain networks than models based solely on spatial constraints. These results provide a controlled computational account showing that functional demands can induce modular organization in artificial recurrent networks under capacity constraints, suggesting modularization as an adaptive response to the sequential introduction of complex tasks. Wu et al. show that neural networks learning multiple tasks organize into specialized modules, particularly under capacity constraints. Incremental multitask learning strengthens this modularity and produces architectures resembling brain networks.
abstract_zh: 理解神经系统如何发展出模块化组织是神经科学和人工智能的基石。人们认为，模块化架构对于适应性和复杂的认知表现至关重要，因为它们丰富了大脑整合和处理信息的能力。虽然先前的研究认为模块化是由物理约束（如最小化代谢连接成本）产生的，但这些仅基于空间的模型单独无法完全解释脑网络的功能组织。一个关键的未解问题是：学习复杂任务的功能需求如何在计算上影响网络拓扑结构？在此，我们利用训练于认知任务的循环神经网络，演示功能需求如何塑造结构组织。我们发现，多任务学习范式相比单任务训练增强了网络的模块化程度，特别是在网络容量受到压力时。特别是采用递进多任务学习的网络，发展出最高程度的模块化，并保持优越的性能。此外，这些由任务诱导的网络表现出的结构特性比仅基于空间约束的模型更接近生物脑网络。这些结果提供了一个受控的计算解释，表明在容量约束下，功能需求可以在人工循环网络中诱导模块化组织，这表明模块化是对复杂任务顺序引入的自适应反应。Wu 等人展示，学习多个任务的神经网络会组织成专门的模块，特别是在容量约束下。递进多任务学习加强了这种模块化，并产生类似脑网络的架构。
